## Setting and conventions

- [P] Section 1 (pp. 2-3): `X = (x_ij)` is an `n x n` skew-symmetric matrix of indeterminates and `R = K[X]`; Definition 1.1 (p. 2): a ladder `Y` of index pairs is symmetric and satisfies the corner condition that
  `(i, j)` and `(h, k)` in `Y` with `i < h` and `j > k` force `(i, k)`, `(i, h)`, `(h, j)` and `(j, k)` into `Y`; a ladder is a union of square subladders `X_k` described by upper corners `(a_k, b_k)`. A `2t`-pfaffian is the pfaffian of a `2t x 2t` submatrix, and Definition 1.2 (p. 3)
  defines the pfaffian ideal of a ladder `I_(2t)(Y)` as the sum of the ideals `I_(2 t_k)(X_k)` for a vector `t = (t_1, ..., t_s)`. Proposition 1.5 (p. 3, from the authors' earlier paper) gives the height of `I_(2t)(Y)` as the number of pairs `(i, j)`, `i < j`, in the ladder `Y-tilde` of Notation 1.4; the earlier paper proves these ideals prime, normal and Cohen-Macaulay.
- [P] Definition 1.6 and Theorem 1.7 (pp. 3-4): `I` is obtained from `I'` by a G-biliaison of height `l` on `J` when `fI + J = gI' + J` with `deg g = deg f + l`; Theorem 1.7 (stated from the authors' earlier paper) gives, for a ladder ideal `I` and its neighbor `I'` obtained by lowering one entry of `t` and moving one upper corner,
  an elementary G-biliaison of height 1 on a third ladder ideal `J`, with `f` a `2(t_k - 1)`-pfaffian and `g` a `2 t_k`-pfaffian (p. 4); p. 3 records that, as a consequence, ladder pfaffian ideals are glicci.
- [P] Notation (pp. 4-7): `L_t^n` is the pfaffian ideal of the ladder with upper corners `(1, n-1)` and `(2, n)` (p. 4); `M_t` is the ideal of the `2t`-pfaffians of a `(2t+1) x (2t+1)` generic skew-symmetric matrix and `SM_t`
  that of a `(2t+2) x (2t+2)` matrix (p. 4); `N_t`, `SN_t`, `L_t(k)`, `L_t(j, k)` and `H_t(j, k)` are the ladder families drawn on pp. 5-6; `I_t^n` is the ideal of the `2t`-pfaffians of an `n x n` generic skew-symmetric matrix (p. 7).

## Theorem statements

- [P] Proposition 2.1 (p. 7): for homogeneous saturated unmixed ideals `H, I, J` with `H` Cohen-Macaulay and `I` obtained from `J` by an elementary G-biliaison of
  height `l` on `H`, the multiplicity satisfies `e(I) = e(J) + l e(H)`.
- [P] Formula (2.1) (p. 7), cited from Krattenthaler: `e(I_t^n) = product over 1 <= i <= j <= n - 2t + 1 of (2(t-1) + i + j)/(i + j)`.
  Formula (2.2) (p. 8): `e(M_t) = 1 + 2^2 + 3^2 + ... + t^2`, cited from Herzog-Trung-Valla and Herzog-Trung.
- [P] Proposition 2.2 (p. 7): a closed formula for `e(L_t^n)`, obtained as `e(I_t^(n+1)) - e(I_(t-1)^(n-1))` from Theorem 1.7, Proposition 2.1 and (2.1).
  Proposition 2.3 (p. 8): `e(L_t(2)) = 1 + sum_(s=2)^t [2s(1 + 2^2 + ... + s^2) - s^3]` and a formula for `e(N_t)`. Corollary 2.4 (p. 9):
  `e(SM_t) = t + sum_(r=2)^t sum_(s=2)^r [2s(1 + 2^2 + ... + s^2) - s^3]`.
- [P] Theorem 2.5 (p. 9): for a ladder `Y = Y_1 union Y_2` whose associated ladders `Y-tilde_1` and `Y-tilde_2` of Notation 1.4 have disjoint sets of indeterminates,
  `e(I) = e(I_1) e(I_2)`. Proposition 2.6 (pp. 9-10): `e(H_t(j, k)) = e(L_(t-1)(j)) e(L_t(k))`. Propositions 2.7 and 2.8 (p. 10): recursive
  formulas for `e(L_t(j, k))` and `e(L_t(k))`; Remarks 2.9 (p. 11) state that the recursion computes every case and that the formula
  of Proposition 2.7 fails for `k = 0`. Proposition 2.10 (p. 11): `e(SN_t) = sum_(s=2)^t e(L_s(1, 2)) + sum_(s=2)^(t-1) s e(SM_s) + 1`.
- [P] Theorem 3.1 (p. 12): for homogeneous Cohen-Macaulay ideals with `I` obtained from `J` by an elementary G-biliaison of height `l` on
  `H` and `reg(J) < reg(H)`, `reg(I) = reg(H) + l - 1`. Proposition 3.2 (p. 13): `reg(L_t(2)) = 3t - 2` and `reg(N_t) = 3t - 4`
  for `t >= 2`. Proposition 3.3 (p. 13): `reg(SM_t) = 3t - 2`. The text states `reg(M_t) = 2t - 1` as well known (p. 12).
- [P] Definition 4.1 and Proposition 4.2 (pp. 14-15): the `h`-vector of `M_t` is of decreasing type; the proof (p. 15) writes `h_(M_t)(m)` as `h_(M_1)(m - t + 1)` plus the sum over `j = 2, ..., t` of shifted `h`-vectors of complete intersections of two forms of degree `j`. Proposition 4.3 (p. 15): the minimal free resolution of `M_t` has the form
  `0 -> R[-2t-1] -> R[-t-1]^(2t+1) -> R[-t]^(2t+1) -> M_t -> 0`.

## Mapping to this repository

- [I] The A_5 program works with Pfaffian ideals and their Rees algebras. The source gives closed numerical invariants of the
  ideal itself, not of its Rees algebra or special fiber: the degree (multiplicity) from Formulas (2.1) and (2.2) and Propositions
  2.2 to 2.10, the regularity from Section 3, and the resolution of `M_t` in Proposition 4.3. A degree or Betti-number check
  of a Pfaffian ideal that appears in the program can start from these values.
- [I] For the generic case `M_t` the Hilbert series follows from Proposition 4.3, with `e(M_2) = 1 + 4 = 5` and `e(M_3) = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14`
  by Formula (2.2); these two values are arithmetic on the paper's formula, not statements printed in it.
- [I] None of the repository ideals is shown to be a ladder pfaffian ideal; the paper applies only to ideals of indeterminate
  pfaffians over a field `K`, so a repository ideal in coordinates of an orbit closure needs a separate argument before any of
  these formulas applies.

## Boundaries

[I] The proofs were read for structure and not rederived. The paper's Betti-number statement covers `M_t` only; the graded
Betti numbers of the other ladder ideals are not computed there. No claim in this note rests on a computation in this repository.
